gen-dafont-bloody-gf-cascadia-code: Bloody swaggers in with big round lowercase bowls and a thick-thin pulse, while Cascadia Code draws everything like bent wire. That difference in stroke is what holds the two together.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-cascadia-mono: Loud, heavy and a bit menacing, Bloody up top gets a body in Cascadia Mono whose strokes never swell or thin. Quiet, almost mechanical company for it.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-julius-sans-one: Bloody comes on commanding, its big round bowls swinging between thick and thin, while Julius Sans One glides beneath like fine wire with wide gaps. Reading it would feel light and spacious.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-exa: Commanding is how Bloody lands, with its big round bowls and shifting stroke, over Lexend Exa's wide, steady curves. The strongest thing here is the gap between a dramatic head and a body that never changes pressure.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-giga: Bloody leads with big round lowercase bowls and a dramatic swing in its strokes, a look quite unlike its partner below. Lexend Giga follows in flat, single-weight lines with generous tracking, so a long block of sans-serif text moves along easily.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads friendly and modern, drawn as if with one nib.  Under Bloody's heavy, swelling bowls it gives the page a steady, open counterweight, with its tall lowercase nearly meeting the capitals.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-peta: Approachable Lexend Peta keeps its strokes uniform, with wide-mouthed c shapes and a big x-height, in a plain sans that never wavers. And Bloody's dramatic, swelling bowls above it make that uniformity feel deliberate rather than dull.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-tera: Bloody opens with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding thick-thin sweep, a loud contrast to its quiet partner. Lexend Tera spaces its letters like stepping stones in a plotter-pen line, so a long page of plain sans would feel unhurried.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-zetta: Bloody commands attention with big round bowls and a bloody, swelling stroke, set against sans lettering cut like ribbon of constant width. Lexend Zetta can take a larger size, since its tall small letters stay open.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-montserrat-alternat: Bloody shows off big round lowercase bowls that swell and thin, while Montserrat Alternates keeps every round letter outlined at a constant width. Paragraphs in that sans would read crisply, though a little crowded toward the capital line.
